# Beamdrop

> Beamdrop is a self-hosted, single-binary file storage server with an S3-compatible REST API built in Go. It replaces cloud storage with a lightweight, zero-dependency solution — web file manager, programmable storage API, presigned URLs, shareable links, real-time stats, and Prometheus metrics in one ~39MB binary.

## Overview

Beamdrop runs as a single binary with zero external dependencies on Linux, macOS, and Windows (Intel + ARM). SQLite database for metadata, filesystem for object storage. Docker image is ~39MB.

Core capabilities:
- **Web UI**: React-based file manager with drag-and-drop upload, search, move, copy, rename, mkdir, trash
- **S3-Compatible API**: Full REST API at `/api/v1/` for buckets, objects, presigned URLs, and API key management
- **Shareable Links**: Token-based URLs with optional bcrypt-hashed password protection, configurable expiry, and access counting
- **Real-time Dashboard**: WebSocket-powered (`/ws/stats`) storage stats, bandwidth metrics, request counters
- **Security**: HMAC-SHA256 API auth, JWT web auth with token revocation, per-IP rate limiting (3 tiers), CSRF protection, CSP headers, TLS support
- **Observability**: Structured JSON logging (slog), Prometheus metrics at `/metrics`, Kubernetes health probes, Grafana dashboard template

## Quick Start

```bash
# Share current directory on auto-detected port (prefers 7777)
beamdrop

# With password protection and S3 API auth
beamdrop -dir /path/to/share -p mysecretpassword -api-auth

# Create an API key (secret shown only once)
curl -X POST http://localhost:7777/api/v1/keys
# Response: {"accessKeyId": "BDK_...", "secretKey": "sk_...", ...}

# Production behind Cloudflare with TLS
beamdrop -dir /data -p secret -api-auth -disable-csp -disable-csrf -tls-cert cert.pem -tls-key key.pem
```

## CLI Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `-dir` | `.` | Directory to share (becomes root for web UI and bucket storage) |
| `-port` | auto (prefers 7777) | Server port. Auto-detection tries 7777 first, then finds available |
| `-p` | none | Password for web UI authentication. Enables JWT-based auth with HttpOnly cookies |
| `-api-auth` | false | Enable HMAC-SHA256 API key authentication for S3 API endpoints |
| `-qr` | false | Generate and display QR code for mobile access on startup |
| `-tls-cert` | none | TLS certificate file path. Enables HTTPS and adds HSTS header |
| `-tls-key` | none | TLS private key file path. Required with `-tls-cert` |
| `-rate-limit` | 100 | General rate limit in requests/min per IP. Auth tier = 5% (5/min). Upload tier = 10% (10/min). Set 0 to disable |
| `-max-storage` | unlimited | Maximum total storage. Accepts human-readable sizes: "500MB", "10GB", "1TB" |
| `-db-path` | `<dir>/.beamdrop/beamdrop.db` | SQLite database path for metadata, API keys, presigned URLs, shareable links |
| `-log-level` | info | Structured log level: debug, info, warn, error |
| `-allowed-origins` | none (CORS disabled) | Comma-separated CORS origins. Empty = CORS disabled (most secure) |
| `-shutdown-timeout` | 30s | Graceful shutdown timeout for in-flight requests |
| `-jwt-secret` | auto-generated | JWT signing secret. Min 32 bytes. Auto-generated and persisted in DB if omitted |
| `-trusted-proxies` | none | Comma-separated CIDR ranges for reverse proxy IP detection (X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP) |
| `-disable-csp` | false | Skip Content-Security-Policy header. Needed for some CDN/proxy setups (e.g., Cloudflare) |
| `-disable-csrf` | false | Skip CSRF token validation. Needed when API clients can't manage CSRF tokens |
| `-disable-system-stats` | false | Hide server disk/memory/CPU stats from the web dashboard |

All flags can be set via `BEAMDROP_*` environment variables (CLI flags take precedence):
`BEAMDROP_DIR`, `BEAMDROP_PASSWORD`, `BEAMDROP_PORT`, `BEAMDROP_DB_PATH`, `BEAMDROP_TLS_CERT`, `BEAMDROP_TLS_KEY`, `BEAMDROP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, `BEAMDROP_API_AUTH`, `BEAMDROP_QR`, `BEAMDROP_LOG_LEVEL`, `BEAMDROP_RATE_LIMIT`, `BEAMDROP_MAX_STORAGE`, `BEAMDROP_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT`, `BEAMDROP_JWT_SECRET`, `BEAMDROP_TRUSTED_PROXIES`, `BEAMDROP_DISABLE_CSP`, `BEAMDROP_DISABLE_CSRF`, `BEAMDROP_DISABLE_SYSTEM_STATS`

## Authentication

### HMAC-SHA256 API Authentication (S3 API)

Enabled with `-api-auth` flag. All `/api/v1/` requests must be signed.

**Key format:**
- AccessKeyID: `BDK_` + 16 hex chars (8 random bytes). Example: `BDK_a1b2c3d4e5f67890`
- SecretKey: `sk_` + 40 hex chars (20 random bytes). Example: `sk_0123456789abcdef...`
- Secret is encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM using a server-derived 32-byte key
- Secret is shown only once at creation — it cannot be retrieved later

**Signing algorithm:**
1. Get current UTC time as RFC3339: `2024-01-15T10:30:00Z`
2. Build string to sign: `METHOD + "\n" + PATH + "\n" + TIMESTAMP`
   - PATH is the URL path only, no query string. Example: `/api/v1/buckets/my-bucket`
3. Compute: `Signature = Base64(HMAC-SHA256(StringToSign, SecretKey))` (standard Base64, not URL-safe)
4. Set headers:
   - `Authorization: Bearer BDK_xxxx:SIGNATURE`
   - `X-Beamdrop-Date: 2024-01-15T10:30:00Z`

**Clock skew tolerance:** ±15 minutes. Requests outside this window are rejected with 401.

**API key properties:**
- `permissions`: JSON string — `"read"`, `"write"`, or `"read,write"`
- `bucketScope`: Optional. Restricts key to operations on a single bucket
- `expiresAt`: Optional. Key automatically stops working after this time
- `disabled`: Boolean. Can be set to temporarily disable a key
- `lastUsedAt`: Tracked automatically on each authenticated request

### Web Authentication (Password-Based)

Enabled when `-p <password>` flag is set. Independent from API auth.

- `POST /auth/login` with `{"password": "..."}` → JWT in `beamdrop_token` HttpOnly cookie (SameSite=Strict)
- `POST /auth/logout` → revokes token immediately (stored in revocation table, checked on each request)
- `GET /auth/status` → check if current session is authenticated
- Password is hashed with bcrypt at cost=10
- Background job cleans up expired revoked tokens

## S3-Compatible API Reference

Base path: `/api/v1/`

### API Keys

**Create API Key**
```
POST /api/v1/keys
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "my-key",
  "permissions": "read,write",
  "bucket_scope": "optional-bucket",
  "expires_in": "720h"
}

Response 201:
{
  "id": 1,
  "name": "my-key",
  "accessKeyId": "BDK_a1b2c3d4e5f67890",
  "secretKey": "sk_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "permissions": "read,write",
  "bucketScope": "optional-bucket",
  "expiresAt": "2024-02-15T10:30:00Z",
  "createdAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "warning": "Save the secret key now — it cannot be retrieved later"
}
```
⚠️ The `secretKey` field is shown ONLY in the creation response. Store it immediately.

**List API Keys**
```
GET /api/v1/keys

Response 200:
{
  "keys": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "name": "my-key",
      "accessKeyId": "BDK_a1b2c3d4e5f67890",
      "permissions": "read,write",
      "bucketScope": "optional-bucket",
      "expiresAt": "2024-02-15T10:30:00Z",
      "lastUsedAt": "2024-01-20T08:00:00Z",
      "createdAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
      "disabled": false
    }
  ],
  "count": 1
}
```
Note: `secretKey` is never returned in list responses.

**Delete API Key**
```
DELETE /api/v1/keys?accessKeyId=BDK_a1b2c3d4e5f67890

Response 204 (no content)
```
Deletion is immediate — any in-flight or future requests using this key will fail with 401.

### Buckets

**Bucket name validation:**
- Regex: `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{1,61}[a-z0-9]$`
- Length: 3-63 characters exactly
- Allowed characters: lowercase a-z, digits 0-9, hyphens `-`, dots `.`
- Must start and end with a letter or digit
- IP-like names rejected (e.g., `192.168.1.1` → INVALID_BUCKET_NAME)
- Valid examples: `my-bucket`, `data.2024`, `ai-artifacts`
- Invalid examples: `-bucket`, `MY-BUCKET`, `ab`, `a-bucket-name-that-is-way-too-long-and-exceeds-the-sixty-three-character-limit`

**List Buckets**
```
GET /api/v1/buckets

Response 200:
{
  "buckets": [
    {"name": "my-bucket", "createdAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z"}
  ],
  "count": 1
}
```

**Create Bucket**
```
PUT /api/v1/buckets/{bucket}

Response 201:
{"bucket": "my-bucket", "created": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z", "location": "/api/v1/buckets/my-bucket"}

Error 409 if bucket already exists:
{"error": {"code": "BUCKET_EXISTS", "category": "CONFLICT", "message": "Bucket already exists"}}
```

**Create Bucket (Idempotent) — RECOMMENDED**
```
PUT /api/v1/buckets/{bucket}?createIfNotExists=true

Response 201 (newly created):
{"bucket": "my-bucket", "created": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z", "location": "/api/v1/buckets/my-bucket"}

Response 200 (already existed):
{"bucket": "my-bucket", "exists": true, "location": "/api/v1/buckets/my-bucket"}
```
Always prefer `?createIfNotExists=true` to avoid 409 errors in automated workflows.

**Check Bucket Existence**
```
HEAD /api/v1/buckets/{bucket}

Response 200 (exists) — no body
Response 404 (not found) — no body
```

**Delete Bucket**
```
DELETE /api/v1/buckets/{bucket}

Response 204 (no content) — bucket successfully deleted
Response 404 — bucket not found
Response 409 — bucket not empty (delete all objects first)
```

### Objects

**Object key validation:**
- Cannot be empty
- Cannot contain `..` (path traversal prevention)
- Cannot start with `/`
- Maximum 1024 bytes (S3 compatible)
- Forward slashes `/` in keys create virtual directory hierarchies
- Valid examples: `file.txt`, `folder/sub/file.pdf`, `2024/01/report.csv`
- Invalid examples: `../etc/passwd`, `/absolute/path`, empty string

**List Objects**
```
GET /api/v1/buckets/{bucket}?list=true&prefix=folder/&delimiter=/&max-keys=100

Response 200:
{
  "bucket": "my-bucket",
  "prefix": "folder/",
  "delimiter": "/",
  "maxKeys": 100,
  "isTruncated": false,
  "contents": [
    {
      "key": "folder/file.txt",
      "size": 1234,
      "lastModified": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
      "etag": "d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e",
      "contentType": "text/plain"
    }
  ],
  "commonPrefixes": [{"prefix": "folder/subfolder/"}]
}
```

**Query parameters:**
- `list=true` — Required to trigger list mode (otherwise treated as object download)
- `prefix` — Filter to objects whose keys start with this string
- `delimiter` — Group objects by this separator. Use `/` for directory-like listing. Objects between prefix and next delimiter occurrence become `commonPrefixes`
- `max-keys` — Maximum number of objects to return (default 1000)

**Upload Object**
```
PUT /api/v1/buckets/{bucket}/{key}
Content-Type: application/octet-stream
Body: <raw file bytes>

Response 200:
{
  "bucket": "my-bucket",
  "key": "path/to/file.txt",
  "etag": "d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e",
  "size": 1234,
  "url": "/api/v1/buckets/my-bucket/path/to/file.txt"
}
```

**Upload details:**
- Maximum file size: 5GB (5,242,880,000 bytes)
- Writes are atomic: temp file → fsync → rename → fsync parent dir. If the server crashes mid-write, the old file is preserved
- ETag is the MD5 hex hash of the uploaded content, computed during write
- Parent directories in the key path are created automatically
- Per-object write locks prevent concurrent writes to the same key (30-second lock timeout)
- Multipart form upload also supported via `POST` with `multipart/form-data`
- Allowed MIME types: images (jpeg, png, gif, webp, svg+xml, bmp), documents (pdf, docx, xlsx, pptx, txt, csv, html, css, js), archives (zip, rar, 7z, tar, gzip), audio (mpeg, wav, ogg, mp4, webm, flac), video (mp4, mpeg, webm, ogg, avi, quicktime), code (json, xml, javascript), application/octet-stream

**Download Object**
```
GET /api/v1/buckets/{bucket}/{key}

Response 200:
Headers:
  Content-Type: text/plain
  Content-Length: 1234
  ETag: "d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e"
  Last-Modified: Mon, 15 Jan 2024 10:30:00 GMT
Body: <raw file bytes>
```

- Supports HTTP `Range` header for partial downloads (e.g., `Range: bytes=0-999`)
- ETag in response headers is quoted (e.g., `"abc123"`); the Go client trims quotes automatically

**Get Object Metadata (HEAD)**
```
HEAD /api/v1/buckets/{bucket}/{key}

Response 200:
Headers: Content-Type, Content-Length, ETag, Last-Modified
(no body)

Response 404 if object not found
```

**Delete Object**
```
DELETE /api/v1/buckets/{bucket}/{key}

Response 204 (no content)
Response 404 if object not found
```

### Presigned URLs

Beamdrop supports two types of presigned URLs. Choose based on your requirements:

**Type 1: Client-side HMAC presigned URLs**
- Generated locally using your secret key — no API call to the server
- Self-contained: all auth info is in the URL query parameters
- Cannot be revoked (valid until expiry or key rotation)
- No download tracking or limits
- Best for: ephemeral links, embedding in emails, cases where you don't need control after generation

```
Token = Base64URL(HMAC-SHA256("METHOD\nBUCKET\nKEY\nUNIX_TIMESTAMP", SecretKey))
URL = https://server/api/v1/buckets/{bucket}/{key}?access_key=BDK_xxx&expires=2024-01-16T10:30:00Z&token=TOKEN
```

Note: Key rotation invalidates ALL client-side presigned URLs generated with the old key.

**Type 2: Server-side pretty presigned URLs (RECOMMENDED for most use cases)**
- Created via API call, stored in database with 32-char hex token
- Short, clean URLs: `/dl/{token}`
- Revocable at any time — revoked URLs return 404 immediately
- Download counting: `downloadCount` tracks usage
- Download limits: `maxDownloads` restricts total uses
- Expiry: `expiresAt` for time-based expiration
- Best for: shareable links, download portals, temporary access, anything requiring control or auditing

**Create Server-Side Presigned URL**
```
POST /api/v1/presign
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "bucket": "my-bucket",
  "key": "path/to/file.txt",
  "method": "GET",
  "expires_in": 3600,
  "max_downloads": 10
}

Response 201:
{
  "id": 1,
  "token": "a1b2c3d4e5f67890a1b2c3d4e5f67890",
  "url": "https://server/dl/a1b2c3d4e5f67890a1b2c3d4e5f67890",
  "bucket": "my-bucket",
  "key": "path/to/file.txt",
  "method": "GET",
  "expiresAt": "2024-01-15T11:30:00Z",
  "maxDownloads": 10,
  "downloadCount": 0,
  "createdBy": "BDK_a1b2c3d4e5f67890",
  "createdAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z"
}
```

**Request fields:**
- `bucket` (required): Target bucket name
- `key` (required): Target object key
- `method` (optional, default "GET"): HTTP method allowed
- `expires_in` (optional): Seconds until expiry. Omit for no expiry
- `max_downloads` (optional): Maximum download count. Omit for unlimited

**List Presigned URLs**
```
GET /api/v1/presign

Response 200:
{"urls": [...], "count": 5}
```

**Get Presigned URL Details**
```
GET /api/v1/presign/{token}

Response 200: (same structure as create response, with updated downloadCount)
```

**Revoke Presigned URL**
```
DELETE /api/v1/presign/{token}

Response 200: {"message": "Presigned URL revoked"}
```
After revocation, `GET /dl/{token}` returns 404 immediately.

**Download via Presigned URL (Public)**
```
GET /dl/{token}

Response 200: file download with Content-Disposition header
Response 404: expired, revoked, or max downloads reached
```
No authentication required — this is the public download endpoint. Supports Range header.

**When to use which presigned URL type:**

| Scenario | Use Client-side | Use Server-side |
|----------|----------------|-----------------|
| Quick temporary link, no tracking needed | ✅ | |
| Need to revoke access after sharing | | ✅ |
| Want to limit number of downloads | | ✅ |
| Need to track how many times a file was downloaded | | ✅ |
| Embedding download links in automated emails | ✅ | |
| Creating a download portal for users | | ✅ |
| Link must survive API key rotation | | ✅ |
| Generating many links with zero server overhead | ✅ | |
| Sharing sensitive files with audit trail | | ✅ |

## Error Responses

All errors follow a consistent JSON structure:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "BUCKET_NOT_FOUND",
    "category": "NOT_FOUND",
    "message": "The specified bucket does not exist",
    "details": {}
  }
}
```

**Complete error code reference:**

| HTTP | Code | Category | Retryable | Description |
|------|------|----------|-----------|-------------|
| 400 | INVALID_REQUEST | VALIDATION | No | Malformed request body or parameters |
| 400 | INVALID_BUCKET_NAME | VALIDATION | No | Bucket name doesn't match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{1,61}[a-z0-9]$` |
| 400 | INVALID_OBJECT_KEY | VALIDATION | No | Key empty, contains `..`, starts with `/`, or >1024 bytes |
| 400 | INVALID_PATH | VALIDATION | No | Request path is invalid |
| 400 | MISSING_FIELD | VALIDATION | No | Required field missing from request |
| 401 | UNAUTHORIZED | AUTH | No | Missing or invalid Authorization header |
| 401 | INVALID_TOKEN | AUTH | No | JWT token is invalid |
| 401 | TOKEN_EXPIRED | AUTH | No | JWT token has expired |
| 401 | INVALID_API_KEY | AUTH | No | API key not found or disabled |
| 401 | API_KEY_EXPIRED | AUTH | No | API key has passed its expiresAt time |
| 403 | FORBIDDEN | AUTH | No | Valid auth but insufficient permissions |
| 403 | PERMISSION_DENIED | AUTH | No | API key lacks required permission for this operation |
| 404 | BUCKET_NOT_FOUND | NOT_FOUND | No | Bucket does not exist |
| 404 | OBJECT_NOT_FOUND | NOT_FOUND | No | Object does not exist in bucket |
| 404 | FILE_NOT_FOUND | NOT_FOUND | No | File not found (web UI operations) |
| 404 | LINK_NOT_FOUND | NOT_FOUND | No | Shareable link token not found |
| 409 | BUCKET_EXISTS | CONFLICT | No | Bucket already exists (use `?createIfNotExists=true`) |
| 409 | BUCKET_NOT_EMPTY | CONFLICT | No | Cannot delete bucket with objects in it |
| 409 | OBJECT_EXISTS | CONFLICT | No | Object already exists (for create-only operations) |
| 413 | FILE_TOO_LARGE | VALIDATION | No | Upload exceeds 5GB limit |
| 415 | INVALID_MIME_TYPE | VALIDATION | No | Content type not in allowed MIME types list |
| 423 | OBJECT_LOCKED | STORAGE | Yes | Object is currently locked by another operation. Retry after brief delay |
| 429 | RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED | RATE_LIMIT | Yes | Per-IP rate limit exceeded. Check `Retry-After` header |
| 507 | STORAGE_FULL | STORAGE | No | Server storage capacity reached (`-max-storage` limit) |

**Retry headers** (present when retryable=true):
- `Retry-After: <seconds>` — number of seconds to wait before retrying
- `X-Retryable: true` — signals that the request can be retried

## Rate Limiting

Token bucket algorithm with three independent tiers per IP address:

| Tier | Endpoints | Default Rate | Burst Capacity |
|------|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| General | All endpoints | 100 req/min | 100 requests |
| Auth | `/auth/login` | 5 req/min | 5 requests |
| Upload | PUT objects, `/upload` | 10 req/min | 10 requests |

- Configure with `-rate-limit N` flag (sets general tier; auth tier = 5% of N, upload tier = 10% of N)
- Disable entirely with `-rate-limit 0`
- Buckets start full and refill continuously
- Stale IP entries cleaned up every 5 minutes (removes IPs unseen for >10 minutes)
- IP extraction: Uses RemoteAddr by default. Only trusts X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP from `-trusted-proxies` list. For X-Forwarded-For, uses the first (leftmost) IP

## Security Headers

Applied to all responses:
```
X-Frame-Options: DENY
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=()
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' ws: wss:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains  (HTTPS only)
```

CSP can be disabled with `-disable-csp` flag (needed for some CDN proxies like Cloudflare).

## CORS

Disabled by default (most secure). When enabled via `-allowed-origins`:
```
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <requested origin if in allowed list>
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, OPTIONS
Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization, X-Request-ID
Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-Request-ID
Access-Control-Max-Age: 86400
```
Preflight OPTIONS requests return 403 if origin is not in the allowed list.

## Health Endpoints

- `GET /health` — Component status (JSON: disk, database, storage)
- `GET /health/live` — Kubernetes liveness probe (always 200 if process is running)
- `GET /health/ready` — Kubernetes readiness probe (checks disk access)
- `GET /health/startup` — Kubernetes startup probe (for slow boot scenarios)
- `GET /ready` — Legacy readiness alias
- `GET /metrics` — Prometheus metrics (request counters, latency histograms, storage gauges)
- `GET /stats` — Real-time storage stats (JSON)
- `GET /ws/stats` — WebSocket for real-time stats streaming

## Storage Internals

**Filesystem layout:**
```
<shared-dir>/
├── buckets/
│   ├── my-bucket/
│   │   ├── file.txt
│   │   └── folder/
│   │       └── nested-file.pdf
│   └── another-bucket/
├── .beamdrop/
│   └── beamdrop.db          (SQLite: API keys, presigned URLs, shareable links, revoked tokens)
└── .trash/                   (soft-deleted files from web UI)
```

**Atomic writes:** Every object write goes through: create temp file (`.beamdrop_tmp_*` prefix) → write content + compute MD5 → fsync file → atomic rename to target → fsync parent directory → return ETag. On failure, temp file is cleaned up and the original object is preserved.

**Object locking:** Per-object read/write locks via `LockManager`. Lock key = `{bucket}/{key}`. Default timeout = 30 seconds. Deadlock detection runs every 10 seconds. Stale lock warnings at 5 minutes. Lock is acquired before write, released after atomic rename completes.

## Go Client SDK

```go
import "github.com/ekilie/beamdrop/pkg/client"

// Initialize — validates BaseURL, creates HTTP client with 2-minute timeout
c, err := client.New(client.Config{
    BaseURL:     "http://localhost:7777",   // Required. Must have scheme and host
    AccessKeyID: "BDK_abc123",             // Optional for anonymous access
    SecretKey:   "sk_secret",              // Required if AccessKeyID is set
    // HTTPClient: custom *http.Client     // Optional, defaults to 2-min timeout
    // UserAgent: "my-app/1.0"             // Optional, defaults to "beamdrop-go-client/0.1"
})

// Buckets
buckets, _ := c.ListBuckets(ctx)                           // → *BucketList{Buckets, Count}
created, _ := c.CreateBucket(ctx, "my-bucket")             // → *BucketCreated — errors on 409 if exists
created, _ = c.CreateBucketIfNotExists(ctx, "my-bucket")   // → *BucketCreated — 201 or 200 with Exists=true
exists, _ := c.BucketExists(ctx, "my-bucket")              // → bool (HEAD request, 404 → false)
_ = c.DeleteBucket(ctx, "my-bucket")                       // → error (409 if not empty)

// Objects
uploaded, _ := c.PutObject(ctx, "bucket", "key", []byte("content"))   // → *ObjectCreated{Bucket,Key,ETag,Size,URL}
uploaded, _ = c.PutObjectReader(ctx, "bucket", "key", ioReader)       // Streaming upload from io.Reader
obj, _ := c.GetObject(ctx, "bucket", "key")                           // → *ObjectBody{ObjectMetadata, Body []byte}
meta, _ := c.HeadObject(ctx, "bucket", "key")                         // → *ObjectMetadata{ContentType,ContentLength,ETag,LastModified}
_ = c.DeleteObject(ctx, "bucket", "key")                              // → error
exists, _ = c.ObjectExists(ctx, "bucket", "key")                      // → bool (HEAD, 404 → false)
list, _ := c.ListObjects(ctx, "bucket", client.ListObjectsOptions{    // → *ObjectList
    Prefix:    "folder/",                                              //   Contents []ObjectInfo + CommonPrefixes
    Delimiter: "/",
    MaxKeys:   100,
})

// Presigned URLs — client-side (HMAC, no server call)
url, _ := c.PresignObjectURL("GET", "bucket", "key", time.Now().Add(24*time.Hour))
// Returns: "http://server/api/v1/buckets/bucket/key?access_key=BDK_xxx&expires=...&token=..."

// Presigned URLs — server-side (database-tracked, revocable)
presigned, _ := c.CreatePresignedURL(ctx, client.CreatePresignedURLRequest{
    Bucket:       "bucket",
    Key:          "key",
    Method:       "GET",
    ExpiresIn:    int64Ptr(3600),    // 1 hour in seconds
    MaxDownloads: intPtr(10),        // limit to 10 downloads
})
// presigned.URL = "https://server/dl/a1b2c3..."
// presigned.Token = "a1b2c3..."

urls, _ := c.ListPresignedURLs(ctx)              // → *PresignedURLList{URLs, Count}
details, _ := c.GetPresignedURL(ctx, "token")    // → *PresignedURL (with current downloadCount)
_ = c.DeletePresignedURL(ctx, "token")           // Revoke — /dl/token immediately returns 404
```

**Error handling in Go client:**
```go
result, err := c.GetObject(ctx, "bucket", "missing-key")
if err != nil {
    var apiErr *client.APIError
    if errors.As(err, &apiErr) {
        fmt.Println(apiErr.StatusCode)  // 404
        fmt.Println(apiErr.Code)        // "OBJECT_NOT_FOUND"
        fmt.Println(apiErr.Category)    // "NOT_FOUND"
        fmt.Println(apiErr.Retryable)   // false
        if apiErr.Retryable {
            time.Sleep(time.Duration(apiErr.RetryAfter) * time.Second)
            // retry...
        }
    }
}
```

**Sentinel errors:** `client.ErrInvalidBaseURL`, `client.ErrMissingCredentials`, `client.ErrInvalidPath`

## MCP Server

Beamdrop includes a built-in MCP server at the `/mcp` endpoint, implemented natively in Go. It uses the Streamable HTTP transport with JSON-RPC 2.0. No separate process or TypeScript build needed — it runs as part of the Beamdrop server.

- `GET /mcp` — Public discovery endpoint (returns protocol version, transport, available methods)
- `POST /mcp` — JSON-RPC 2.0 request processing (requires API key auth, same HMAC-SHA256 as S3 API)

**MCP Configuration for AI assistants:**

```json
// Claude Desktop — claude_desktop_config.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "beamdrop": {
      "url": "https://your-server.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer BDK_your_key:signature",
        "X-Beamdrop-Date": "ISO-8601-timestamp"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**Available tools (16 total):**

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| `list_buckets` | none | List all storage buckets |
| `create_bucket` | `name`, `idempotent?` | Create a bucket (idempotent by default) |
| `delete_bucket` | `name` | Delete an empty bucket |
| `bucket_exists` | `name` | Check if a bucket exists |
| `list_objects` | `bucket`, `prefix?`, `delimiter?`, `maxKeys?` | List objects with S3-style filtering |
| `put_object` | `bucket`, `key`, `content`, `isBase64?` | Upload text or base64-encoded binary |
| `get_object` | `bucket`, `key` | Download object (text or base64 for binary, 10MB limit) |
| `head_object` | `bucket`, `key` | Get object metadata |
| `delete_object` | `bucket`, `key` | Delete an object |
| `create_presigned_url` | `bucket`, `key`, `method?`, `expiresIn?`, `maxDownloads?` | Create revocable download link |
| `list_presigned_urls` | none | List all presigned URLs |
| `get_presigned_url` | `token` | Get presigned URL details |
| `delete_presigned_url` | `token` | Revoke a presigned URL |
| `list_api_keys` | none | List API keys (no secrets) |
| `create_api_key` | `name?`, `bucketScope?`, `permissions?` | Create new API key |
| `delete_api_key` | `id` | Delete an API key |

## Webhooks

Beamdrop supports real-time event notifications via webhooks. Register HTTP callback URLs and receive signed POST requests when events occur.

**Webhook Management API:**
- `POST /api/v1/webhooks` — Create webhook (returns signing secret once)
- `GET /api/v1/webhooks` — List all webhooks
- `PATCH /api/v1/webhooks/{id}` — Update webhook (name, url, enabled, event_types, bucket_scope, rotate_secret)
- `DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/{id}` — Delete webhook and all delivery history
- `POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/test` — Send a synthetic test event
- `GET /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` — List recent delivery attempts

**Event Types:**
| Event | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `beamdrop.object.created` | Object uploaded or created |
| `beamdrop.object.updated` | Object content updated |
| `beamdrop.object.deleted` | Object deleted |
| `beamdrop.bucket.created` | Bucket created |
| `beamdrop.bucket.deleted` | Bucket deleted |
| `beamdrop.share.created` | Shareable link created |
| `beamdrop.share.deleted` | Shareable link deleted |
| `beamdrop.presign.created` | Presigned URL created |
| `beamdrop.presign.deleted` | Presigned URL revoked |

Wildcards: `beamdrop.object.*`, `beamdrop.bucket.*`, `beamdrop.share.*`, `beamdrop.presign.*`

**Webhook Signing:**
Beamdrop signs every webhook delivery with HMAC-SHA256:
```
signature_base = timestamp + "\n" + delivery_id + "\n" + request_body
signature = "v1=" + hex(HMAC-SHA256(signature_base, webhook_secret))
```

Headers sent with each delivery:
- `X-Beamdrop-Webhook-Id` — Webhook ID
- `X-Beamdrop-Event` — Event type (e.g., `beamdrop.object.created`)
- `X-Beamdrop-Delivery-Id` — Unique delivery UUID
- `X-Beamdrop-Timestamp` — Unix timestamp
- `X-Beamdrop-Signature` — `v1=hex_signature`

**Delivery behavior:**
- Up to 8 retry attempts with exponential backoff (2s base, 15min max)
- Retryable HTTP status codes: 408, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504
- 10-second request timeout per delivery attempt
- Failed deliveries after max attempts are marked as dead_letter
- Delivery history retained for 7 days

**Create webhook example:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://server/api/v1/webhooks \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer BDK_xxx:signature" \
  -H "X-Beamdrop-Date: 2024-01-15T10:30:00Z" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"my-hook","url":"https://example.com/webhook","event_types":["beamdrop.object.*"]}'
# → {"webhook":{...}, "secret":"whsec_...", "warning":"Save the secret now — it will not be shown again."}
```
